$comment: The authoritative fight clock (Rule 8 / Rule 9). schemas/clock_settings.schema.json has existed since Phase 0 with nothing behind it, and 'accelerated-clock synchronization' is one of the ROADMAP's eleven required automated checks - one of the three that could not run because there was no clock to test. This defines it: one clock, read by everything, with the Accelerated Clock changing only the mapping between displayed and real time and never the tick that the simulation runs on. Engine-neutral definitions only (Rule 18). Semantics: docs/phase1a/authoritative_clock.md.

authority.notes: Rule 9: every system reads one clock. A second clock anywhere is how a corner ends up on a different schedule from the referee.

accelerated_clock.$comment: Rule 8, exactly as stated: ON displays 3:00 over 1:45 of real time. It is a presentation mapping, not a simulation speed change.
accelerated_clock.notes: The count clock is deliberately exempt: a knockdown count is a safety instrument and runs on real seconds whatever the display says.

prohibitions: Run a second clock anywhere in the simulation or presentation (Rule 9).
Let the Accelerated Clock change the simulation tick rate, authored frame data, stamina per tick or the knockdown count clock (Rule 8).
Permit free-form round lengths outside the authored set (Rule 8).
Let menus pause the between-rounds break (Rule 8).
Let wall-clock time drive the authoritative simulation (Criterion E.19).

invariants.statement: A single authoritative clock is read by simulation, judging, officiating, corners, presentation and replay alike.
The Accelerated Clock changes the mapping between displayed and real time and nothing else - not the tick rate, not frame data, not stamina, not the count.
Accelerated display is 3:00 over 1:45 of real time, the ratio PROJECT_RULES states.
Rounds are one, two or three minutes; free-form lengths are prohibited.
The between-rounds break is thirty real seconds and menus do not pause it, matching the condition model.
The knockdown count is exempt from acceleration; a safety instrument does not speed up because the display does.
Wall-clock time never drives the simulation.
